43632379.article_content:
The chroot Technique - a Swiss army multitool for Linux systems
April 8, 2025
Ever ran into a Linux box that just won’t boot, even after making sure that
BIOS settings are OK and that no major hardware errors are at hand?
Then you need to know about the
chroot
technique, which can be a real life
saver.
For example, I managed to repair a
Nanopore GridION device
this way the other week, after the
official method of re-installing it via an .iso file
failed, which reminded me to make the effort of documenting these steps.
I came across the technique only after having used Linux as my daily driver for
more than a decade (thanks
Matt
!), which means I
think it is worthy of much more attention, given its usefulness. Thus I’m
hoping to spread the word a bit through this post.
TLDR
In short, the idea is that if you can access the hard drive of a broken or
non-bootable Linux machine (this could be done e.g. by booting from a Live
USB-stick, or plugging in the hard-drive as an extra drive in another Linux
machine), you will mount this hard drive in a way that you trick your current
Linux session that this is the harddrive of the currently running system, which
it is not of course.
The trick to get this to work is to create a file tree based on two things:
The hard drive partition of the broken system that was mounted as the
/
folder
on the host operating system.
A set of special system folders from the currently running, temporary,
operating system (the live stick or replacement computer), which are not
normal directories on the disk, but rather are containing system information
needed by the running linux system. These include
/sys
,
/proc
and a few
others, which we will go into details about below.
Then what you do is that you run the
chroot
command on this newly assembled
folder structure, meaning that your currently running linux session will
replace its current file system with this new blend of folders, mostly from the
old, broken, hard drive.
It is a bit like hooking up a malfunctioning car to externally provided power
source so that you can at least access its instrumentation, check the mileage,
any error codes on the display etc.
Anyways, what this lets you do is then to run various commands that could
hopefully repair or diagnose your system, such as
apt upgrade
,
dpkg-reconfigure
for broken packages on Debian based systems, or something
else, depending on the specifics of your system.
The process
It is good to have the full process for setting up the assembled folder
structure and doing the chroot, in one place, so that you can easily find it
when you need it.  Optimally you would even print out a small cheatsheet with
these commands, or have them stored in a text file on your “repair toolkit” USB
stick, or similar.
Anyways, below you will find all the steps of the process:
Boot up your replacement OS (A live USB stick, or other computer with the broken
computer’s hard drive attached to it).
Figure out which partition on the broken system’s hard drive holds the root
file system, and which one holds the
/boot
folder.
I typically use
gparted
for that, which is available on most Ubuntu/Linux Mint
based live disks.
You can also use command-line based tools like
sudo fdisk -l
I typically try to mount each of the broken system’s partitions into the
file navigator (they typically show up as mountable drives in Thunar i
Linux Mint XFCE) to really make sure I select the right partition.
If you are not able to do that, you will have to do some guessing based on
filesystem size and type, whether they are already available in
/etc/fstab
etc.
In this example, we will assume that the root folder is in partition:
/dev/nvme0n1p5
… and that the
/boot
partition is in:
/dev/nvme0n1p3
(These happen to be the case for the Nanopore GridION device I mentioned
that I repaired this way recently).
Create a folder somewhere in your currently running system’s file system, that will
act as the new root folder, as well as the
/boot
folder inside that:
sudo mkdir /rescue
sudo mkdir /rescue/boot
Mount the broken system’s main and boot partitions into these folders, e.g:
sudo mount /dev/nvme0n1p5 /rescue
sudo mount /dev/nvme0n1p3 /rescue/boot
Then, mount in the required special folders from your currently running
system, into the appropriate places in this new file structure (the
mount
command is on the form
mount -t <file-system-type> -o <options> <device> <mount-point>
)
sudo mount -t proc proc /rescue/proc
sudo mount -t sysfs sys /rescue/sys
sudo mount -o bind /dev /rescue/dev
sudo mount -t devpts pts /rescue/dev/pts
Now we are ready to
chroot
, or “change rootfolder” into this newly created
folder structure:
chroot /rescue /bin/bash -i
And we’re done!
Now you can look around in the file system to try to figure out what is causing
the system to not work, as well as use whatever file commands you need to try
to repair the broken system,
In our case with the broken GridION device, we found some broken symlinks and
empty
initrd.img-*
files

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：音频录制设备和麦克风对录音质量的影响

不同观点：
• MrJagil认为音频录制设备对录音质量有重要影响，并提到Zoom F3是新的主力设备，Sony PCM D100则是已停产的经典设备。他表示这些设备在行业内被广泛认可，说明专业人士能够辨别音质好坏。

• kazinator指出，该比较仅针对录音硬件设备，而非麦克风。他提到，虽然有一些使用不同麦克风录制的音频样本，但并没有对麦克风进行量化比较，仅对录音设备进行了定量分析。

• pier25表示，虽然该资源非常有用，但录音中的噪音主要来源于麦克风本身。他以Rode NT1麦克风为例，指出在录制非常安静的音源时，没有听到来自前置放大器的任何噪音。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于录音质量的关键因素。MrJagil强调录音设备的作用，而pier25则认为麦克风对噪音的影响更大。

• kazinator的评论提醒读者注意比较的对象，强调了区分录音设备和麦克风的重要性，以避免混淆两者对音质的影响。

• pier25的实际使用经验为讨论提供了具体的例子，强调了麦克风选择在减少噪音方面的重要性。

data.title: The Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: 谷歌云推出了一种名为Agent2Agent（A2A）的新开放协议，旨在实现AI代理之间的互操作性。该协议允许不同厂商或框架开发的代理安全通信、交换信息并协调行动，从而提升企业的自动化水平和生产效率。A2A支持多种模式，包括音频和视频流，并基于现有标准如HTTP、SSE和JSON-RPC，方便与现有系统集成。关键设计原则包括代理能力发现、长周期任务支持和默认安全机制。通过与50多家技术伙伴合作，A2A将帮助企业在不同平台和云环境中统一管理AI代理，实现跨应用协作，推动企业创新和工作流自动化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕A2A和MCP协议的讨论，涉及其功能、必要性、安全性及未来应用场景

不同观点：
• **AndrewKemendo** 认为，这些协议的目的是通过"搜索"功能将用户的数据控制在公司手中，从而长期依赖这些数据建立竞争壁垒（moat）。随着公开数据的获取趋同，公司更加渴望获取用户的私有数据以保持优势。
• **simonw** 关注MCP协议的安全性问题，特别是提示注入攻击（prompt injection attacks），指出虽然协议本身无明显漏洞，但其使用模式可能带来安全隐患。
• **zurfer** 质疑是否需要完全规范的协议，提出是否可以通过REST API和最佳实践来替代A2A和MCP协议，从而实现类似的功能。
• **zellyn** 表示希望看到更简单的示例和实际的JSON数据交换过程，认为当前协议描述令人困惑，且对协议的某些背书反而使其显得更复杂。
• **johnnythunder** 设想未来通过AI代理订阅服务实现不同级别的功能，高级的模型和代理将需要更高的费用，同时开源社区会提供非订阅的自定义功能。
• **LeonidBugaev** 简要解释A2A和MCP的区别，强调A2A侧重于代理之间的任务通信，具有任务状态和通知功能，而MCP更多是请求-响应模式的工具通信。
• **pjmlp** 提到Agent Tcl的历史，暗示当前的AI代理讨论可能是在重新发现过去的技术和架构，如SOA和WSDL。
• **hliyan** 同样将当前的AI代理协议与过去的软件架构（如SOA和WSDL）类比，建议软件工程教育中加入历史课程，以避免重复过去的错误。
• **peterjliu** 质疑A2A是否是为了在MCP之后推出以保持竞争优势，并提出代理和工具的概念可能互换。
• **flakiness** 指出A2A和MCP的区别在于A2A保持多个交互的连接，而MCP更像是纯粹的请求-响应模式。
• **rahulcap** 认为A2A和MCP的胜负取决于它们能否给开发者信心以实现完全自主的模式。
• **dleeftink** 提出可以进一步抽象化候选人搜索过程，通过微交易市场来寻找最优候选人。
• **jason-phillips** 对协议的细节感到失望，认为其仅提供了显而易见的JSON描述，并没有太多创新。
• **trash_cat** 展望未来个人代理的广泛应用，尤其是在处理官僚和非官僚任务方面，并指出更强大的代理将需要付费。
• **vessenes** 对A2A和MCP进行了详细比较，认为A2A在解决MCP痛点方面做得更好，建议如果要构建MCP服务器，应参考A2A的规范，A2A是MCP的合理扩展。

补充讨论：
• 安全性是讨论中的一个重要关注点，特别是提示注入攻击（simonw, vessenes）。
• 关于是否需要完全规范的协议存在争议，部分人认为可以通过现有技术实现类似功能（zurfer, hliyan, pjmlp）。
• 协议的应用场景和未来发展方向也是讨论的重点，尤其是个人和企业代理的广泛应用（johnnythunder, trash_cat, rahulcap）。
• A2A和MCP的具体区别和优势是另一个讨论焦点，特别是它们在任务通信和工具通信方面的不同（LeonidBugaev, flakiness, vessenes）。
• 部分讨论者对协议的实际应用效果和文档质量提出了具体意见（zellyn, jason-phillips, vessenes）。

Announcing the Agent2Agent Protocol (A2A)
APR 09, 2025
Rao Surapaneni

A new era of Agent Interoperability
AI agents offer a unique opportunity to help people be more productive by autonomously handling many daily recurring or complex tasks. Today, enterprises are increasingly building and deploying autonomous agents to help scale, automate and enhance processes throughout the workplace–from ordering new laptops, to aiding customer service representatives, to assisting in supply chain planning.
To maximize the benefits from agentic AI, it is critical for these agents to be able to collaborate in a dynamic, multi-agent ecosystem across siloed data systems and applications. Enabling agents to interoperate with each other, even if they were built by different vendors or in a different framework, will increase autonomy and multiply productivity gains, while lowering long-term costs.
Today, we’re launching a new, open protocol called Agent2Agent (A2A), with support and contributions from more than 50 technology partners
like Atlassian, Box, Cohere, Intuit, Langchain, MongoDB, PayPal, Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow, UKG and Workday; and leading service providers including Accenture, BCG, Capgemini, Cognizant, Deloitte, HCLTech, Infosys, KPMG, McKinsey, PwC, TCS, and Wipro. The A2A protocol will allow AI agents to communicate with each other, securely exchange information, and coordinate actions on top of various enterprise platforms or applications. We believe the A2A framework will add significant value for customers, whose AI agents will now be able to work across their entire enterprise application estates.
This collaborative effort signifies a shared vision of a future when AI agents, regardless of their underlying technologies, can seamlessly collaborate to automate complex enterprise workflows and drive unprecedented levels of efficiency and innovation.
A2A is an open protocol that complements Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides helpful tools and context to agents. Drawing on Google's internal expertise in scaling agentic systems, we designed the A2A protocol to address the challenges we identified in deploying large-scale, multi-agent systems for our customers. A2A empowers developers to build agents capable of connecting with any other agent built using the protocol and offers users the flexibility to combine agents from various providers. Critically, businesses benefit from a standardized method for managing their agents across diverse platforms and cloud environments. We believe this universal interoperability is essential for fully realizing the potential of collaborative AI agents.
A2A design principles
A2A is an open protocol that provides a standard way for agents to collaborate with each other, regardless of the underlying framework or vendor. While designing the protocol with our partners, we adhered to five key principles:
Embrace agentic capabilities
: A2A focuses on enabling agents to collaborate in their natural, unstructured modalities, even when they don’t share memory, tools and context. We are enabling true multi-agent scenarios without limiting an agent to a “tool.”
Build on existing standards:
The protocol is built on top of existing, popular standards including HTTP, SSE, JSON-RPC, which means it’s easier to integrate with existing IT stacks businesses already use daily.
Secure by default
: A2A is designed to support enterprise-grade authentication and authorization, with parity to OpenAPI’s authentication schemes at launch.
Support for long-running tasks:

data.title: Show HN: Dynomate– Fast, Git-Friendly DynamoDB GUI Client (Dynobase Alternative)
data.author: orlando252
data.article_summary: Dynomate是一款现代化的DynamoDB图形界面客户端，专为无服务器团队设计，提供SSO、多会话、多标签支持、请求链等功能。它与AWS无缝集成，支持简单的一键SSO登录和配置文件管理，具备多区域、多表管理及查询工具。用户可以通过表格视图或JSON数据进行查看和编辑，支持本地请求持久化和Git集成，方便团队协作。此外，它提供操作链功能，可顺序或并行执行多个查询，并具备详细的请求日志，帮助开发者调试和优化。目前适用于macOS，Windows和Linux版本即将推出。专业许可证价格为199美元，包含一年的更新服务。

data.title: SpacetimeDB
data.author: matthewfcarlson
data.article_summary: SpacetimeDB是一个结合了关系数据库和服务器功能的平台，允许开发者直接将应用逻辑部署到数据库中，无需复杂的运维基础设施。它简化了多人游戏和应用的开发过程，通过编写SpacetimeDB模块并编译为WebAssembly上传，即可实现包括实时状态和持久化在内的全套后端功能。其设计灵感来自数据导向编程和ECS架构，支持ACID特性，确保应用状态的原子性、一致性、隔离性和持久性。SpacetimeDB抽象了云环境的复杂性，使开发者可以像操作单台逻辑计算机一样处理分布式系统，特别适合构建大规模多人在线游戏和应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SpacetimeDB的技术特点、应用场景及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• **jackb4040**：认为SpacetimeDB尽管看起来不错，但实际上是一个为低延迟优化的传统数据库，缺乏运动预测或多版本控制等高级游戏特性。用户需要自行处理网络延迟掩盖（lag masking）的代码。
• **aeturnum**：将SpacetimeDB归类为需要开发者重新调整思维方式的"宇宙大脑重组"技术之一，类似于Elixir和Node。这类技术的成功依赖于是否有明确的愿景和成功的开源项目来展示其优势。对SpacetimeDB能否实现其承诺持观望态度。
• **bob1029**：作为SpacetimeDB的开发者或支持者，强调该数据库是为大规模多人在线游戏（MMO）设计，具备极低延迟和高吞吐量的特性。并指出当前市场中如《魔兽世界》的实例，表明通过巧妙处理客户端信任和服务器事件调和可以实现扩展。

补充讨论：
• **kriper**：质疑如何在使用SpacetimeDB的情况下编写游戏服务器，尤其是如何处理物理模拟、路径规划和动画等功能，是否需要放弃游戏引擎重新实现这些功能。
• **paulluuk**：表示对SpacetimeDB的实际应用价值不确定，虽然宣传很吸引人，但不清楚其中有多少是营销效果。
• **weego**：对SpacetimeDB及其游戏BitCraft表示兴趣，但对其定价术语"maincloud"产生个人偏见，担心涉及加密货币相关内容，后发现是托管信用命名问题。
• **_huayra_**：指出SpacetimeDB是BSL许可项目，限制较多，比如每个服务只能有一个实例，可能影响扩展性。
• **ksynwa**：询问是否有关于在线游戏使用技术的资料，表示对后台技术不了解。
• **vivzkestrel**：关注如何将SpacetimeDB与Unreal Engine 5.5集成。
• **arittr**：误以为SpacetimeDB是由Spaceteam开发者推出的项目。
• **beders**：反对将关系数据库模式与应用程序数据处理混为一谈，主张显式控制而非注解魔法。
• **thefourthchime**：对SpacetimeDB在实际应用中的效果表示好奇，通过YouTube视频了解后仍持保留态度。
• **matthewfcarlson**：认为SpacetimeDB结合了关系型数据库和无服务器计算，并对其快速更新持怀疑态度。
• **xixixao**：指出"数据库内服务器"模型类似于Convex，但Convex更适合JS全栈应用。

争议焦点：
• SpacetimeDB是否如宣传那样具备颠覆性和实用性，还是只是传统数据库的优化版本。
• 如何在实际游戏开发中有效集成SpacetimeDB，尤其是与现有游戏引擎（如Unreal/Unity）的兼容性问题。
• SpacetimeDB许可模式对其扩展性的限制是否会影响其广泛应用。

Modern database environment
SpacetimeDB takes stored procedures to the next level, allowing you to deploy your whole app directly into the database. It's like a smart contract... if smart contracts were fast, cheap, and easy to use.

Deploy your entire application.
Relational database environment
The Cloud Operating System
You can think of SpacetimeDB as an operating system for the cloud. Just as your PC operating system abstracts away the hardware, SpacetimeDB abstracts away the complexities of managing many physical machines in the cloud, allowing you to treat them a single logical computer running one big distributed operating system.
Beautifully generalized
The category of applications that we call games spans anywhere from Solitare to Among Us to World of Warcraft. The only systems versatile enough to serve as an engine for games are databases. SpacetimeDB doesn't constrain you to match making, or real-time movement, or guns, or characters.
ACID everything
Every update to your application state is 100% atomic, consistent, isolated, and durable. You get to write your game logic inside single-threaded, atomic functions which are called directly from clients, while we multi-thread *everything* behind the scenes. You have access to all of your application state through indexed, in-memory relational tables that are defined by your application.
Data-oriented and ECS inspired
The design and architecture of SpacetimeDB is highly influenced by a data oriented approach to programming. Writing Entity-Component-System applications is both natural and extremely performant in SpacetimeDB. • **kriper**：质疑如何在使用SpacetimeDB的情况下编写游戏服务器，尤其是如何处理物理模拟、路径规划和动画等功能，是否需要放弃游戏引擎重新实现这些功能。
• **paulluuk**：表示对SpacetimeDB的实际应用价值不确定，虽然宣传很吸引人，但不清楚其中有多少是营销效果。
• **weego**：对SpacetimeDB及其游戏BitCraft表示兴趣，但对其定价术语"maincloud"产生个人偏见，担心涉及加密货币相关内容，后发现是托管信用命名问题。
• **_huayra_**：指出SpacetimeDB是BSL许可项目，限制较多，比如每个服务只能有一个实例，可能影响扩展性。
• **ksynwa**：询问是否有关于在线游戏使用技术的资料，表示对后台技术不了解。
• **vivzkestrel**：关注如何将SpacetimeDB与Unreal Engine 5.5集成。
• **arittr**：误以为SpacetimeDB是由Spaceteam开发者推出的项目。
• **beders**：反对将关系数据库模式与应用程序数据处理混为一谈，主张显式控制而非注解魔法。
• **thefourthchime**：对SpacetimeDB在实际应用中的效果表示好奇，通过YouTube视频了解后仍持保留态度。
• **matthewfcarlson**：认为SpacetimeDB结合了关系型数据库和无服务器计算，并对其快速更新持怀疑态度。
• **xixixao**：指出"数据库内服务器"模型类似于Convex，但Convex更适合JS全栈应用。

争议焦点：
• SpacetimeDB是否如宣传那样具备颠覆性和实用性，还是只是传统数据库的优化版本。
• 如何在实际游戏开发中有效集成SpacetimeDB，尤其是与现有游戏引擎（如Unreal/Unity）的兼容性问题。
• SpacetimeDB许可模式对其扩展性的限制是否会影响其广泛应用。

43631004.article_content:
React for Two Computers April 9, 2025 I’ve been trying to write this post at least a dozen times. I don’t mean this figuratively; at one point, I literally had a desktop folder with a dozen abandoned drafts. They had wildly different styles—from rigoruous to chaotically cryptic and insufferably meta; they would start abruptly, chew on themselves, and eventually trail off to nowhere. One by one, I threw them all away because they all sucked. It turns out that I wasn’t really writing a post; I was actually preparing a talk. I was pretty far into the process of writing this post when I had that realization. Oops! Thankfully, the React Conf organizers let me present a new talk on a short notice, and I did that eight months ago. You can watch React for Two Computers below. It’s about everyone’s favorite topic, React Server Components. (Or maybe not.) I’ve given up on the idea of converting this talk into a post form, nor do I think it’s possible. But I wanted to jot down a few notes that are complementary to the talk. I’m going to assume that you have watched the talk itself. This is just the stuff that wasn’t coherent enough to make the cut—the loose threads I couldn’t tie together. Act 1 Recipes and Blueprints What is the difference between a tag and a function call? Here’s a tag: < p > Hello Here’s a function call: alert ( ' Hello ' ); One difference is that < and > are hard and spiky and ( and ) are soft and round. But that’s not what I mean. These are just visual differences. But what is the difference in how they work, what they mean, in what we expect from them? Of course, there is no particular meaning to a tag or a function call if you don’t specify which language you’re using. For example, a JavaScript function call might not behave the same way as a Haskell function call; an HTML tag might not behave the same way as a ColdFusion tag. Nevertheless, there are some things that we expect from a tag or a function call precisely because we’re familiar with how they work in popular languages. The spiky < and > carry a set of associations and intuitions, just like the soft ( and ) do. I want to dig into these intuitions. Let’s start with what alert('Hello') and

Hello

have in common: We refer to a function or a tag by its name. By convention, a function call often starts with a verb ( createElement , printMoney , querySelectorAll ), while tags are usually named with nouns (like p for a paragraph ). This isn’t a hard rule ( alert is both; b stands for bold ) but it’s true more often than not. (Why is that?) We can pass information to a function or a tag. Earlier, we were passing a piece of text ( 'Hello' ) to the tag and the function. But we’re not limited to passing a single string. Within a JavaScript function call, we can pass multiple arguments including strings, numbers, booleans, objects, and so on. Within an HTML tag, we can pass multiple attributes, but their values cannot be objects or other rich data structures—which is quite limiting. Thankfully, tags in JSX (as well as in many HTML-based template languages) let us pass objects and any other rich values. Both function calls and tags can be deeply nested. For example, we could write alert('Hello, ' + prompt('Who are you?')) to express the relationship between these two different function calls: the result of the inner prompt call gets combined with a string, and is then passed to the outer alert call. (Try it in your console if you’re not sure what this does.) Although nesting is fairly common with function calls, with tags nesting really is the name of the game. You hardly ever see a tag completely alone and not surrounded by other tags. (Why is that?) Clearly, function calls and tags are very similar. They let us pass some information to a named thing, and if needed, they let us elaborate by nesting further (passing some more information to some named thing (nesting as much as we need (yay!))) We’re also starting to get a few hints of the fundamental differences between them. For one, function calls tend to be verbs while tags tend to be nouns. Also, you’ll encounter deeply nested tags more often than deeply nested function calls. What’s up with that? Let’s start with the latter. Why do tags tend to cling to each other? Are tags just naturally predisposed to gravitate towards other tags until they— yoink! —click together? Perhaps those spiky bois really do yearn for connection? That may be so, but consider this: maybe we like to use tags for deeply nested structures because we can see the of every tag and don’t have to guess which ) is closing. Tags don’t lead to deep nesting—rather, we choose to use tags for deep nesting. (Recall how broadly the JavaScript community eventually adopted JSX despite it being almost universally panned for a year or two. Nesting tags is hard to give up!) Okay, let’s say we prefer to use tags for nesting. But why do tags tend to be nouns rather than verbs? Is this a coincidence, or is there a deeper

data.title: An LLM Query Understanding Service
data.author: softwaredoug
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要介绍了如何利用LLM（大语言模型）快速改进搜索功能，将复杂查询分解为关键维度，从而实现结构化搜索。作者提到，使用简单的LLM可以在几天内完成以往需要数月的工作，且无需依赖OpenAI或Gemini等外部服务，可以通过本地基础设施运行LLM，提高速度并降低成本。

文章详细描述了如何通过FastAPI部署一个调用LLM的应用，并以Qwen2-7B模型为例展示了如何使用PyTorch调用轻量级LLM。此外，文章还介绍了如何创建Docker镜像，并将其部署到Google Kubernetes Engine（GKE）的自动驾驶模式中。

最后，文章提醒了可能遇到的节点分配问题及相应的Kubernetes操作步骤，如查看和描述pod状态，确保正确分配GPU资源。如果配额不足，可能会导致pod无法分配到合适的节点。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：利用大型语言模型（LLM）将搜索查询转换为结构化搜索过滤器的技巧及其技术细节

不同观点：
• simonw: 通过在多个LLM上测试，如Gemini 1.5 Flash 8B、Llama 3.2 3B和deepseek-r1:1.5b，发现不同模型在处理结构化搜索过滤器时的表现各异。Gemini 1.5 Flash 8B表现良好且成本低廉，Llama 3.2 3B作为本地小模型也能胜任，而deepseek-r1:1.5b则给出了错误答案。所有测试均通过llm.datasette.io平台及相关插件完成。

• MarkSweep: 建议使用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能，以提高生成有效JSON并符合预期架构的可能性。提供了相关API文档链接，如Gemini API和Ollama API，以帮助实现这一功能。

补充讨论：
• hamelsmu: 赞赏Doug在搜索领域的贡献，提到其著作《Relevant Search》并对其重新教授相关知识表示高兴。这一评论更侧重于对Doug个人的认可和对相关知识传播的支持。

争议焦点：
• 不同LLM模型在处理结构化数据时的性能差异，尤其是deepseek-r1:1.5b给出了错误答案，这表明在选择模型时需考虑其准确性和可靠性。
• 是否采用LLM API的“结构化输出”功能以提高JSON输出的有效性，这涉及技术实现的选择和优化。

总结：讨论主要围绕如何利用LLM将搜索查询转换为结构化过滤器以及各模型的表现差异，同时提出了技术优化建议和相关知识的传播。

We need to be cheating at search with LLMs. Indeed
I’m teaching a whole course on this in July

With an LLM we can implement in days what previously took months. We can take apart a query like “brown leather sofa” into the important dimensions of intent — “color: brown, material: leather, category:couches” etc. With this power

Even better we can do this all without calling out to OpenAI/Gemini/…. We can use simple LLMs running in

I’m going to show you how. Let’s get started. Follow along
in this repo
.
The service - wrapping an open source LLM

The Docker Image
To create a kubernetes pod, we need a Docker image with our app. One dependency is a headache with Docker - PyTorch.  Luckily someone has written a great article on
shrinking pytorch images

our Dockerfile

(If you don’t have a Google Cloud account, you can

这篇文章主要介绍了如何利用LLM（大语言模型）快速改进搜索功能，将复杂查询分解为关键维度，从而实现结构化搜索。作者提到，使用简单的LLM可以在几天内完成以往需要数月的工作，且无需依赖OpenAI或Gemini等外部服务，可以通过本地基础设施运行LLM，提高速度并降低成本。

文章详细描述了如何通过FastAPI部署一个调用LLM的应用，并以Qwen2-7B模型为例展示了如何使用PyTorch调用轻量级LLM。此外，文章还介绍了如何创建Docker镜像，并将其部署到Google Kubernetes Engine（GKE）的自动驾驶模式中。

最后，文章提醒了可能遇到的节点分配问题及相应的Kubernetes操作步骤，如查看和描述pod状态，确保正确分配GPU资源。如果配额不足，可能会导致pod无法分配到合适的节点。

data.title: Small Town America vs. Big Box Stores
data.author: spking
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了美国小镇上的本地商店与大型连锁店（如Dollar General）之间的竞争。华盛顿综合商店（Washington General Store）是缅因州一家由Sean和Amy Donaghy夫妇经营的本地商店，不仅提供日常用品，还成为社区居民聚集和交流的地方。然而，一家大型Dollar General即将开业，引发了当地居民的担忧，他们害怕这会对小镇的独特性和经济生态造成破坏。

研究表明，连锁店往往会挤垮本地商家，限制新鲜食品的供应，并从本地经济中抽走财富。尽管一些本地企业如新奥尔良的Mike's Hardware通过差异化经营成功生存下来，但大多数小商家很难与连锁店竞争。大型零售商还通过政府补贴和税收优惠获得不公平的优势，进一步威胁本地经济。文章呼吁保护本地商业，让资金在社区内循环。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dollar General等大型连锁店与本地社区商店之间的竞争及其社会价值。

不同观点：
• alibrarydweller认为Dollar General通过压缩价值主张到单一维度——低价，赢得了市场，但忽略了社区商店在多维度上的价值，比如赞助公园或根据社区需求精选商品。他们认为社会需要一种“无损算法”，既能高效享受连锁店的便利，又能保留本地商店的多样性价值。

• iambateman对Strong Towns理念表示支持，但反对将Dollar General视为“骗局”。他认为消费者选择Dollar General是因为其价格更低，这是市场的自然结果。他建议小型企业应通过独特价值与大企业竞争，同时可以通过政治手段争取补贴以支持本地企业，而不是简单抱怨大企业的不公平优势。

• briandear质疑“我们”是谁，认为社区应自行决定在哪里购物。如果Dollar General提供了更好的价格，消费者自然会选择它。他们指出，要求对Dollar General施加限制实际上是剥夺了低收入人群的选择权，因为这些人依赖于低价商品。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于Dollar General的低价策略是否是一种“骗局”以及社区是否有权自行决定其购物选择。
• alibrarydweller强调了多维度价值和无损算法的重要性，而iambateman和briandear则更关注市场选择和消费者自主权。
• iambateman提出通过政治手段和合作组织争取对小型企业的支持，以对抗大企业的优势。
• briandear提醒注意不应将个人偏好强加于经济上处于不利地位的人群。

43632459.article_content:
Small Town America vs Big Box Stores
"That sense of identity and place that homegrown businesses create—that’s what we want to preserve here," Sean Donaghy told
the local news back in February.
In 2013, Sean and his wife, Amy, purchased the building that now houses the Washington General Store. More than just a place to pick up essentials, the store has become a gathering space where locals can grab a hot meal or stock up on everything from chainsaw oil to craft beer. Their customers include farmers, out-of-towners, and a motley crew of regulars. “Someone will come in and brighten my day, or I’ll brighten theirs just by a conversation,” Sean said. “You think it’s just small talk, but it’s more than that—it builds relationships.”
The Washington General Store in Maine.
But now, much of what the Donaghy’s love about their town is under threat. A 4,000-plus-square-foot Dollar General is slated to open in this town of fewer than 2,000 people. "It absolutely detracts from what Washington is and hopes to be," Sean said. Kathleen Gross, another local, put it bluntly: "We don't want a corporate, faceless box store coming in with no stake in our community."
The concern isn’t just about the immediate hit to small business revenues. Local farmer Jeffrey Knox worries about the broader impact on Washington’s economic ecosystem: "We want our money to stay local, and we like to invest in each other and our community.”
The Big Box Swindle
The residents of Washington are right to fear that a big-box store like Dollar General would take a lot and give very little in return. A
2023 report by the Institute for Local Self-Reliance
(ILSR) found that in both small towns and larger urban settings, dollar stores push out local grocers and other retailers. In doing so, they limit access to fresh food, siphon wealth from local economies, foster crime and violence, and undermine the long-term resilience of the communities they enter. Put another way, the convenient access to low-cost goods comes at a steep price.
“
We want our money to stay local, and we like to invest in each other and our community.
”
Yet over the last five years, Dollar General has opened over 3,500 new locations, including more than 100 in New York, nearly 200 in Ohio, and 300 in Texas. This expansion has brought the total number of Dollar General stores to over 18,000, solidifying its position as the largest retailer in the U.S. by store count. Looking ahead, the company plans to further grow its network, aiming for more than 51,000 outlets in the coming years.
Some argue that the rapid expansion is simply the chain fulfilling fast-growing demand. When Dollar General first arrives and shoppers choose it over the homegrown alternative, this is no different than the market expressing its preferences. As the saying goes: “evolve or die.” That’s what
one hardware store in New Orleans, Louisiana
did to remain competitive with the growing number of big box retailers in the vicinity.
“We feed off of what they don’t do, they can’t do,” the owner of Mike’s Hardware & Supply explained. Part of that looks like emphasizing his longtime staff’s expertise. Another part of it is simply providing goods you can’t find anywhere else. “We don’t sell barbecue pits or lawn mowers, but we have a lot of hard-to-find specialty items, especially in plumbing, that they don’t have,” the owner added. “We’ve evolved to our niche.”
While Mike's Hardware has successfully carved out a space amidst larger-than-life competitors, the real problem with the competition between Dollar General and mom-and-pop stores is that the playing field isn't level. Few will be as lucky as Mike’s.
In fact, a key driver behind the rise of big-box retailers is the extensive government support they receive, including subsidies and billions of dollars to fund their expansion, says Stacey Mitchell, co-director of the ILSR. In
an episode of the Strong Towns podcast
, she explains how companies like Walmart or Target convince local officials that they’re bringing jobs and financial benefits to the area often in exchange for tax breaks and subsidies to cover the cost of land or construction. Unfortunately, many local governments are too quick to take the bait.
Walmart, for example, received subsidies for
one out of every three stores it built
, pocketing over a billion dollars from local governments. A
Dollar General in Haven, Kansas
demanded the taxpayers of the town of less than 2,000 inhabitants to foot the store’s $72,000 utility bill on the promise of jobs and tax revenue. That’s how much it cost to run Haven’s public library and pool for the year. The town caved and subsidized approximately half the bill.
ILSR also discovered that large corporations benefit from tax loopholes, enabling them to avoid paying income taxes in about half the states they operate in. Meanwhile, small businesses don’t have that luxury—they pay taxes on 100% of their earnings.

data.title: Man pages are great, man readers are the problem
data.author: WhyNotHugo
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了man页面的功能和当前阅读器的局限性。虽然man页面实际上支持链接和跨参考（如`.Xr`和`.Sx`宏），并且在转换为HTML时这些链接是可点击的，但常用的man页面阅读器（如`man(1)`命令结合`less(1)`）并不支持显示或跟随这些链接。此外，当前的阅读器也无法在调整终端窗口大小时重新排版文本。文章呼吁开发更好的man页面阅读器，既能支持链接功能，又能实现文本重排，从而提升用户体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于man pages格式、工具及其现代化改进的讨论

不同观点：
• **blueflow**：认为man pages的编写语言（mdoc和mandb）难以掌握，文档不完整，提议在构建过程中将man pages转换为Markdown，利用Markdown工具链来简化编写过程。但也指出Markdown本身存在不统一的问题，不同工具的解析规则和功能集各异。
• **taeric**：反对将man pages转换为Markdown，认为现有的man pages具有丰富的功能，Markdown在处理链接和语义方面不如现有的解决方案，最终可能导致重复复杂化的过程，类似于从XML迁移到JSON后又试图为JSON添加命名空间。
• **tomxor**：支持使用Vim的ft-man-plugin来改善man pages的阅读体验，特别是其对链接和缩进的处理，相较于默认的less工具有显著优势。
• **jordemort**：推荐使用pinfo工具查看man pages和info页面，该工具具有类似lynx的交叉引用导航功能。
• **ksynwa**：希望man pages阅读器能够直接跳转到特定命令行参数的描述部分，目前需要通过正则表达式搜索实现。
• **jasonjmcghee**：建议使用bat工具为man pages提供语法高亮，以提高可读性。
• **amelius**：提议将man pages全部转换为HTML格式，以实现现代化。
• **tasn**：强烈支持用Markdown替代man pages，认为man pages在界面和编写体验上都不如Markdown，尤其对于习惯于现代文档格式的开发者而言。

补充讨论：
• **sjmulder**：指出许多web版本的man pages排版不佳，但OpenBSD的mandoc驱动的在线man pages是个例外，具有良好的排版。
• **mplanchard和kazinator**：提到Emacs和Vim在man pages阅读和导航方面的优势，例如Vim的K命令可以直接打开光标下单词的man page，以及man page阅读器可以记住上次阅读的位置。
• **NoSalt**：认为man pages需要更多示例，以帮助用户更好地理解命令的使用方法。
• **pjmlp**：指出有许多X Windows的man pages阅读器，但未被提及，可能是个问题。
• **kccqzy**：介绍如何在macOS和Linux上将man pages转换为PDF，利用其支持链接和良好排版的特性。

• 是否应将man pages转换为Markdown或HTML等现代格式，以简化编写和阅读体验（blueflow、taeric、tasn等不同观点）。
• Markdown是否具备足够的统一性和功能性来替代man pages格式（blueflow和tasn的不同看法）。

43631672.article_content:
TLDR: man pages support links, but man page readers neither display nor allow
allow following them.
Frequent criticisms of man pages are “they don’t have links to each other” and
“they don’t re-flow if I make the window narrower”. These are perfectly valid
complains, but the reality is that man page do support these features: it’s the
programs that we use to read man pages that don’t implement them.
The format
[
permalink
]
Man pages are stored in the
mdoc(7)
format and in the legacy
man(7)
format
1
. The actual format for these files isn’t the easiest to read in
the world, but it’s definitely not worse than XML or JSON. mdoc has purely
semantic markup. A portion of an mdoc man page looks something like the
following
2
:
.Sh NAME
.Nm openrc
.Nd stops and starts services for the specified runlevel
.Sh SYNOPSIS
In this case
.Sh
,
.Nm
and
.Nd
are macros which mark the following text as
“section header”, “document name” and “document description” respectively. If
you try to manually read or edit these files you’ll need the to consult the
macro overview
.
References (“links”)
[
permalink
]
Two macros are of particular interest:
.Xr
: “Cross reference”: link to another manual page.
.Sx
: Reference to another section in the same manual page.
Both of these can be rendered as links. In fact, when
mdoc(7)
pages are
converted into HTML, both of these macros are converted into actual links. Both
of the above linked manual pages include examples of this. The
.Sh
(section
header) macro renders as an anchor, so links can point to it directly.
Ironically, the documentation for
mdoc(7)
renders links when displayed as HTML
on a browser, but not when displayed in a terminal via the
man(1)
command.
Conclusion
[
permalink
]
We need better man page readers. Ones that let us follow references as links.
Currently
man(1)
formats a man pages and pipes it to
less(1)
. We can’t
easily add supports for links here: we need a pager which understands man pages
natively.
While we’re at it, we could also re-flow text when the terminal window is made
narrower.
When I say legacy here, I really mean it. Documentation for
man(7)
indicates that it was used from 1979 to 1989, and
mdoc(7)
first appeared
in the early 1990s, in 4.4BSD.
↩︎
This sample was copy-pasted from
OpenRC’s man pages
. See the
repository for a full example and licence details.
↩︎

data.title: PDP-11/Hack de luxe
data.author: JPLeRouzic
data.article_summary: 本文描述了作者对PDP-11/Hack计算机的改进过程。由于对之前的面包板版本不满意，并且希望深入了解DCJ11的工作原理，作者设计了一款基于Eurocard的DCJ11单板计算机（SBC）。新版本的PDP-11/Hack增加了扩展槽，升级为"PDP-11/Hack de luxe"。作者展示了新构建的原型机，尽管仍是试验品并需要一些修正，但它已经可以通过USB转串口/TTL适配器连接到控制台，且功耗低于200mA。该SBC使用TH集成电路和标准TTL逻辑，具备字节写入解码、上电解码、复位按钮和复位逻辑等功能。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43629899.article_content:
C
cbscpe
Experienced Member
Joined
Apr 11, 2017
Messages
386
Location
Switzerland
Not really satisfied with my breadboard attempt to build another PDP-11/Hack and also because I wanted to investigate a little bit more how the DCJ11 really works I decided to make another PDP-11/Hack. So I designed a Eurocard DCJ11 based Singleboard Computer. The PCBs arrived today and so nothing better then set them to use. But this time the PDP-11/Hack comes with an expansion slot. So with a proper PCB and the option to expand the SBC it has now become a "PDP11/Hack de luxe"
Here is a picture of the recently built unit
It is still a prototype and as expected already required an ECO. But not to bad for a start. If you ask what is this cable attached to the right, this is a USB to Serial/TTL adapter that connects to the console. As the complete computer draws less than 200mA the adapter also provides power via USB. And below the output of the mandatory PDP-11/Hack test program.
Sorry for the bad picture of the screenshot, but I think you get the idea. As a change of pace I used a real DC319 as the UART. The SBC only uses TH ICs. SMD parts are only used for the capacitors and resistors. Also I only used standard TTL logic. Byte writes are decoded properly, Power-Up is decoded and the 74HCT541 provides a defined power-up configuration and it comes with a reset button and a reset logic as well.
Cheers
Peter

data.title: Show HN: Webtor – open-source torrent streaming engine
data.author: vintikzzzz
data.article_summary: Webtor.io 是一个在线工具，允许用户通过三个简单步骤将种子文件或磁力链接转换为直接下载链接，而无需使用种子客户端。用户可以上传种子文件并获取下载链接，支持选择性文件下载、视频和音频在线流媒体播放，且无大小限制。它还提供 Chrome 扩展，支持将种子打包为 ZIP 档案下载，并具备开发者友好的 SDK。Webtor.io 通过 HTTPS 协议传输数据，用户无需开启 VPN，下载行为对 ISP 不可见，确保匿名和安全。该服务提供 7 天免费试用，支持移动设备使用，所有组件均为开源，遵循 MIT 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开源的种子下载及流媒体服务的合法性与托管问题

不同观点：
• [toomuchtodo的观点]  
  - 该服务类似于put.io的开源版本，非常酷。  
  - 提到需要考虑托管种子的司法管辖区，建议列出对托管远程种子组件友好、忽略版权主张和版权方警告信的托管商。

• [harvey9的观点]  
  - 质疑如果使用托管服务进行流媒体播放，服务提供方是否会因为成为版权内容的传播者而面临被关闭或封锁的风险，尤其是在严格执行版权法律的司法管辖区。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于该服务的法律风险，特别是在不同司法管辖区下，服务提供方是否会被视为版权内容的"分发者"。  
- toomuchtodo关注服务的技术实现和托管环境的选择，强调在版权友好的司法管辖区托管以避免问题。  
- harvey9则担心该服务在一些严格执行版权法的地区是否能够持续运作，担心法律风险可能导致服务被关闭或限制。  
- 两者都提到了版权问题，但toomuchtodo侧重于如何规避风险，而harvey9则关注法律风险对服务本身的潜在影响。

data.title: Brazil's government-run payments system has become dominant
data.author: jcartw
data.article_summary: 2020年11月，巴西央行推出Pix数字支付系统，迅速在疫情期间走红。Pix以即时、免费和易用等特点，取代了现金和银行卡，成为巴西最受欢迎的支付方式。到2024年，Pix年交易量达630亿笔，交易金额达26万亿雷亚尔（约4.5万亿美元）。尽管Pix革新了巴西陈旧的银行业，但也引发了对央行权力过大的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：巴西Pix支付系统的优势、潜在问题以及与其他国家类似系统的比较

不同观点：
• **Pix系统的优势与便捷性**：
  - SwiftyBug：Pix在巴西非常普及，从微小金额到购房都可以使用，速度快且可靠，优于加密货币。
  - pedrovhb：Pix在巴西便捷、免费、跨行即时到账，技术上令人印象深刻，且用户体验良好。
  - bestouff：相对于美国公司垄断，更倾向于政府运营的支付系统，如Pix。

• **政府运营支付系统的潜在问题**：
  - nirui：对比中国支付宝，质疑商业化支付系统的广告和贷款推销问题，认为政府运营系统更可靠。
  - pedrovhb：担心Pix让央行掌握过多用户信息，存在奥威尔式监控的潜在风险。
  - c7b：指出央行数字货币（CBDC）可能带来的问题，如用户体验复杂和金融稳定性担忧。

• **Pix系统对游客的不便**：
  - cyberclimb：Pix系统对游客不友好，因需要巴西身份证号（CPF），在旅游场景中使用受限。

• **与其他国家系统的比较**：
  - seanalltogether：认为政府应资助数字货币的支付基础设施，探讨微交易免费易转移的互联网发展可能性。
  - DanielHB：瑞典的类似系统Swish和BankID由私营组织管理，技术上更先进，且用户体验更好。
  - sparin9：印度的UPI系统与Pix类似，且在更大规模上运行。

• **市场解决方案与公共服务的讨论**：
  - kubb：认为有时不需要市场解决方案，一个适用于所有人的免费系统更便宜、更容易。
  - c7b：Pix和UPI是央行进入零售支付空间的成功案例，但质疑大多数央行将支付系统与CBDC绑定的做法。

补充讨论：
• **Pix对巴西金融系统的影响**：
  - HeavyStorm：巴西金融技术在欺诈频发和政府复杂金融规则的推动下发展迅速，Pix之前已有TED和Boleto等系统。

• **现金回潮现象**：
  - Galatians4_16：尽管全球向无现金社会迈进，但2024年巴西现金使用量回升，原因包括网络安全威胁、金融隐私担忧和经济不稳定。

争议焦点：
• **Pix系统带来的隐私和监控风险**：部分用户担心Pix让央行掌握过多信息，存在潜在的监控风险，而另一部分用户则认为其便捷性和技术可靠性更重要。

• **政府运营与商业化支付系统的优劣**：对比政府运营支付系统的可靠性与商业化系统的广告推销问题，讨论哪种模式更优。

43620279.article_summary: 2020年11月，巴西央行推出Pix数字支付系统，迅速在疫情期间走红。Pix以即时、免费和易用等特点，取代了现金和银行卡，成为巴西最受欢迎的支付方式。到2024年，Pix年交易量达630亿笔，交易金额达26万亿雷亚尔（约4.5万亿美元）。尽管Pix革新了巴西陈旧的银行业，但也引发了对央行权力过大的担忧。
43620279.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：巴西Pix支付系统的优势、潜在问题以及与其他国家类似系统的比较

不同观点：
• **Pix系统的优势与便捷性**：
  - SwiftyBug：Pix在巴西非常普及，从微小金额到购房都可以使用，速度快且可靠，优于加密货币。
  - pedrovhb：Pix在巴西便捷、免费、跨行即时到账，技术上令人印象深刻，且用户体验良好。
  - bestouff：相对于美国公司垄断，更倾向于政府运营的支付系统，如Pix。

• **政府运营支付系统的潜在问题**：
  - nirui：对比中国支付宝，质疑商业化支付系统的广告和贷款推销问题，认为政府运营系统更可靠。
  - pedrovhb：担心Pix让央行掌握过多用户信息，存在奥威尔式监控的潜在风险。
  - c7b：指出央行数字货币（CBDC）可能带来的问题，如用户体验复杂和金融稳定性担忧。

• **Pix系统对游客的不便**：
  - cyberclimb：Pix系统对游客不友好，因需要巴西身份证号（CPF），在旅游场景中使用受限。

• **与其他国家系统的比较**：
  - seanalltogether：认为政府应资助数字货币的支付基础设施，探讨微交易免费易转移的互联网发展可能性。
  - DanielHB：瑞典的类似系统Swish和BankID由私营组织管理，技术上更先进，且用户体验更好。
  - sparin9：印度的UPI系统与Pix类似，且在更大规模上运行。

• **市场解决方案与公共服务的讨论**：
  - kubb：认为有时不需要市场解决方案，一个适用于所有人的免费系统更便宜、更容易。
  - c7b：Pix和UPI是央行进入零售支付空间的成功案例，但质疑大多数央行将支付系统与CBDC绑定的做法。

补充讨论：
• **Pix对巴西金融系统的影响**：
  - HeavyStorm：巴西金融技术在欺诈频发和政府复杂金融规则的推动下发展迅速，Pix之前已有TED和Boleto等系统。

• **现金回潮现象**：
  - Galatians4_16：尽管全球向无现金社会迈进，但2024年巴西现金使用量回升，原因包括网络安全威胁、金融隐私担忧和经济不稳定。

争议焦点：
• **Pix系统带来的隐私和监控风险**：部分用户担心Pix让央行掌握过多信息，存在潜在的监控风险，而另一部分用户则认为其便捷性和技术可靠性更重要。

• **政府运营与商业化支付系统的优劣**：对比政府运营支付系统的可靠性与商业化系统的广告推销问题，讨论哪种模式更优。

data.article_summary: LetterLinks是一款每日单词构建挑战游戏，玩法类似于Scrabble。玩家需用每日提供的字母 tile 在棋盘上构建单词，通过战略性排列获取最高分。游戏棋盘上有特殊方格（如DL、TL、DW、TW）可增加得分。玩家必须将字母 tile 连接成有效的字典单词，所有 tile 必须相连，且单词至少两个字母长。游戏还包括万能牌（Wild cards）和奖励 tile，可增加额外分数。每日有相同的字母供所有玩家挑战，并可通过完成每日奖励挑战获得更高分数。游戏结束后，玩家可提交分数并参与排行榜。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[对一个游戏的评论，涉及用户体验、技术问题、游戏功能和一些幽默互动]

不同观点：
• [积极反馈] 一些用户对游戏给予了积极评价，称赞其用户界面（UI）流畅，游戏反应灵敏，并表达了对游戏的喜爱。
  - [例子] "Very slick UI. Had a lot of fun playing, it was very reactive." （y-curious）
  - [例子] "I love it, thanks!" （RandomBacon）

• [技术问题] 有用户报告了在设备上遇到的技术问题，例如无法在iPad上拖动字母。
  - [例子] "I seem to be unable to tap or drag letters on my iPad - can’t figure out any way to place them on the grid." （jrmg）

• [功能建议] 一些用户对游戏功能提出了建议，例如建议关闭瓦片洗牌功能以减少PVP元素。
  - [例子] "Would recommend that you switch off the tile shuffle feature. Makes it less of a pvp game." （spaceman_2020）
  - [例子] "I'd love to be able to see the boards of people on the leader board." （yaba_money）

• [幽默互动] 部分评论以幽默方式参与讨论，例如模仿下一个投稿标题或调侃排行榜分数。
  - [例子] "Next submission: I built a mom, but my word game doesn’t like her!" （Crosseye_Jack）
  - [例子] "Looks like someone tweaked the leaderboard: there's a score of 1234.5 today." （imglorp）

补充讨论：
• [内部笑话] 评论中包含了对Hacker News用户的内部笑话，增加了评论区的趣味性。
  - [例子] "I love the inside joke for hacker news addicts in the submission title." （fimdomeio）

• [排行榜讨论] 用户对排行榜的分数和可见性表现出兴趣，并提出了查看其他玩家棋盘的愿望。
  - [例子] "I'm in 3rd place!" （drcongo）
  - [例子] "I'd love to be able to see the boards of people on the leader board." （yaba_money）

争议焦点：
• 评论中没有明显的争议，但有用户对游戏功能（如瓦片洗牌）存在不同看法，可能影响游戏的PVP性质。
  - [例子] "Would recommend that you switch off the tile shuffle feature. Makes it less of a pvp game." （spaceman_2020）

总体来看，评论主要集中在对游戏的积极反馈、技术问题、功能建议和一些幽默互动上。

Welcome to LetterLinks! This word-building game gives you a daily
challenge to create words on a game board, similar to Scrabble.
You'll receive a set of letter tiles and need to arrange them
strategically to score points.
At the bottom of the screen, you'll find your letter tiles. Each
letter has a point value (shown in the corner). To play, either
drag a tile or tap to select it, then tap a board position to
place it.
The game board is where you'll place your tiles. To maximize
points, use special squares: DL (Double Letter), TL (Triple
Letter), DW (Double Word), and TW (Triple Word). Important: The
center star square must have a tile placed on it before you can
submit your score.
Form valid dictionary words by placing tiles adjacent to each
other, reading left-to-right or top-to-bottom. All tiles must
connect to each other - no isolated groups allowed. Words must be
at least two letters long.
Look for special tiles in your rack! Wild cards (with a * symbol)
can represent any letter - tap to select which letter you want.
Some days, you might also get bonus tiles that double the score of
the entire word they're part of.
Check out the daily bonus challenge by tapping the gift icon (🎁)
in the top-right corner. Each day features a special word pattern
that earns bonus points! Words that qualify for the daily
challenge will be highlighted and earn 1.5× or 2× more points.
Once you've arranged your tiles, tap "Submit Words" to score them.
Invalid words will be highlighted in red. Your goal is to score as
many points as possible with the available tiles. Try to use all
your tiles for maximum points!
After submitting, you'll see your final score and can enter your
name for the daily leaderboard. Each day brings a new challenge
with the same tiles for everyone, so you can compare your skill

data.title: Tesla Solar Sales Declined for 4 Qtrs. Then Tesla Stopped Publishing the Numbers
data.author: elsewhen
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了特斯拉自2016年收购SolarCity后，在太阳能屋顶业务上的表现。作者曾看好此次收购，认为两家公司有巨大协同效应和销售潜力。然而，特斯拉在推广太阳能产品方面的努力不足，导致其太阳能安装量持续下滑。自2022年第四季度安装100兆瓦后，特斯拉的太阳能安装量连续四个季度下降，且之后不再公布具体数据。与收购后的初期相比，特斯拉的太阳能业务大幅萎缩，安装量远低于2016和2017年的峰值。作者对这一趋势表示失望，认为这不利于清洁技术的发展，呼吁特斯拉加大太阳能业务的努力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特斯拉在住宅太阳能市场中的表现和挑战

不同观点：
• **[boringg]** 认为住宅太阳能面临多重经济挑战，包括关税、公共事业公司的政策变化（如加州CPUC调整NEM政策）、能源储存主要作为保险产品而非经济产品，以及公共事业公司增加费用和减少现场发电的好处。此外，优质客户已经开发殆尽，现在需要争取更难触及的客户。
• **[legitster]** 提到特斯拉收购SolarCity后，马斯克取消了营销预算，依赖于免费的社交媒体宣传，但实际上并未对太阳能业务进行有效推广。
• **[sleepytimetea]** 指出特斯拉的面板和安装总价过高，缺乏竞争力，只有对Powerwall有热情的客户才会购买。相比之下，其他品牌的面板价格更低，且EG4的储能产品表现出色。
• **[i80and]** 回忆特斯拉曾大力推广太阳能，但后来逐渐减少了相关宣传，这种变化令人不解。
• **[vintagedave]** 质疑特斯拉太阳能安装量与其市场潜力不符，指出美国整体太阳能安装量在增长，而特斯拉的100兆瓦安装量显得微不足道，并询问该公司太阳能部门是否具有良好声誉。
• **[timmg]** 作为潜在客户，询问对特斯拉太阳能的非政治性意见，并寻求安装面板和电池的建议。
• **[tensility]** 质疑特斯拉是否实际安装了许多太阳能瓦片。
• **[skc]** 认为太阳能瓦片是一个 brilliant idea，但经济性不佳。
• **[jmyeet]** 将特斯拉视为“meme stock”，从财务角度质疑其整体业务，包括太阳能。指出特斯拉收购SolarCity是拯救一家失败的公司，并预测特斯拉可能被迫通过罢免CEO自救。
• **[resters]** 从政治角度批评特斯拉创始人支持特朗普，认为这影响了公司的严肃性。
• **[looofooo0]** 认为单户住宅的太阳能经济性存疑，且集成光伏屋顶将屋顶功能与光伏功能耦合，可能导致问题，而普通面板能保护屋顶并延长其寿命。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点包括特斯拉太阳能产品的经济性和市场策略，特别是与竞争对手相比的价格和性能。
- 公共政策和公共事业公司的角色也被认为是影响住宅太阳能市场的重要因素。
- 对特斯拉太阳能部门的声誉和未来发展存在质疑。

I have to put my hands up — when Tesla acquired SolarCity in 2016, I supported the decision. Yes, Elon Musk was chairman of both companies. Yes, it was his cousins who were CEO and CTO, and had founded the company based on a suggestion from Elon Musk at Burning Man. Yes, Tesla was saving SolarCity financially in key ways. Nonetheless, I thought there was superb synergy between the companies and huge potential for more solar sales through the Tesla brand, sales network, and customer base.
Since then, Tesla has done some good stuff, but I have to say that I’ve been very disappointed in Tesla’s rather mild, disconnected, and overall lame efforts to sell more rooftop solar power.
Something I noticed a while back proved the point. Tesla’s quarterly rooftop solar power installations started dropping, and dropping, and dropping. At some point, I realized this had gone from an up & down segment of Tesla’s business to a long-term, significant decline.
I decided to go back and actually see how long Tesla had been seeing its solar business decline. Unfortunately, the findings weren’t uplifting. After it’s “last good quarter,” the 4th quarter of 2022, when 100 megawatts (MW) of solar power were installed, Tesla’s rooftop solar installations declined for at least 4 consecutive quarters. The company published the numbers for those 4 quarters, but then, in the next quarter,
Q1 2024
, Tesla simply lamented that its solar installations had declined year over year but stopped publishing those figures. Presumably, the rooftop solar sales decline continued — otherwise, Tesla would have highlighted a return to growth. But we just can’t be certain of that in every quarter.
In the “Assets” section of Tesla’s quarterly financial reports, the company does still publish “Solar energy systems, net.” And the totals for that have continued to decline in every quarter since then. So, if we presume continued quarter-over-quarter declines in solar power installations, that would be 8 straight quarters of decline (not making a judgement on Q1 2025 yet, but I’m not hopeful about that quarter either).
Aside from recent quarters, if you look at the full chart and graph above, it certainly stands out that Tesla’s solar installations have dropped off a cliff compared to where they were right after the SolarCity acquisition. In Q4 2016, 201 MW of solar power were installed. In Q1 2017, 150 MW were installed. In Q2 2017, 176 MW were installed. And then Tesla never got close to those figures again. In Q3 2017, 109 MW of solar power were installed, and Tesla has only broken 100 MW of new solar power capacity in a quarter twice since then.
The trend in those four quarters of 2023 — the last quarters Tesla published that data for — was bad, very had. If that trend continued in 2024, we have to assume Tesla’s solar business is a shell of what it was several (or even a few) years ago.
This is horrible to see for anyone cheering on cleantech growth. Much more solar power needs to be installed, and a massive slowdown in solar installations from a large company like Tesla just doesn’t make sense to me. Even not trying hard, it seems like the company should be able to find many customers ready to take the solar plunge.

43631402.article_summary: 本文讨论了特斯拉自2016年收购SolarCity后，在太阳能屋顶业务上的表现。作者曾看好此次收购，认为两家公司有巨大协同效应和销售潜力。然而，特斯拉在推广太阳能产品方面的努力不足，导致其太阳能安装量持续下滑。自2022年第四季度安装100兆瓦后，特斯拉的太阳能安装量连续四个季度下降，且之后不再公布具体数据。与收购后的初期相比，特斯拉的太阳能业务大幅萎缩，安装量远低于2016和2017年的峰值。作者对这一趋势表示失望，认为这不利于清洁技术的发展，呼吁特斯拉加大太阳能业务的努力。

data.title: CSS Naked Day
data.author: rpgbr
data.article_summary: CSS Naked Day是每年4月9日举行的一项活动，旨在通过暂时移除网站的CSS样式，展示网页标准的重要性，包括正确的HTML使用、语义标记和良好的结构层次。参与方式简单，只需在4月9日移除网站的所有CSS文件，以“裸露”页面示人。该活动持续50小时，以确保全球不同地区的访问者都能看到无样式的网页。活动由Dustin Diaz在2006年发起，目前由Fabien Basmaison和Jens Oliver Meiert维护。此外，还有各种工具和插件支持不同平台的开发者参与。
data.comments_summary:

• panstromek指出在自己的一个网站上，去除CSS会导致性能问题，尤其是带有无限滚动行为的水平轮播组件会变成不断加载的垂直列表，强调了需要修复的技术问题。
• desdenova质疑为何网站在讨论去除CSS的情况下还会使用CSS，暗示可能不必要或不合时宜。
• internetter分享了自己网站上通过代码根据不同时区自动去除CSS的趣味做法，并附上了代码链接作为例子。

43630957.article_content:
April 9 is CSS Naked Day!
Join us for the yearly festivities on April 9 of going nude on the Web!
The idea behind CSS Naked Day is to promote web standards. Plain and simple. This includes proper use of HTML, semantic markup, a good hierarchy structure, and of course, a good old play on words. In the words of 2006, it’s time to show off your <body> for what it really is.
CSS Naked Day editions
2025
2024
2023
2022
2021
2020
2019
2018
2017
2016
2015
2014
2013
2012
2011
2010
2009
2008
2007
2006
How to participate
On April 9, simply remove all CSS from your website, stripping it entirely of its design.
You can link to this page to let your visitors know about the nudity of your website! This option is for those who feel a need to give their visitors a reference as to what’s going on. This is not about getting traffic or making money. There are no ads on this site, nor will there ever be. This is about you, the people; getting naked.
You can instead add your website(s) here by
creating an issue
or
updating the proper file
! Note:
Alphabetical order
should prevent merge conflicts.
Don’t think, just strip
Here is a sample PHP function for developers:
<?php
function is_naked_day($d) {
$start = date('U', mktime(-14, 0, 0, 04, $d, date('Y')));
$end = date('U', mktime(36, 0, 0, 04, $d, date('Y')));
$z = date('Z') * -1;
$now = time() + $z;
if ( $now >= $start && $now <= $end ) {
return true;
}
return false;
}
?>
Use it like this:
<head>
…
<?php
if ( is_naked_day(9) ) {
echo '<!-- Naked Day has no styles -->';
} else {
echo '<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css" />';
}
?>
…
</head>
Wait… isn’t that 50 hours?
That’s correct. CSS Naked Day lasts for one international day. Technically speaking, it will be April 9 somewhere in the world for 50 hours, from
00:00, April 9 UTC+14:00
to
00:00, April 10 UTC-12:00
(
10:00, April 8 UTC+00:00
to
12:00, April 10 UTC+00:00
). This is to ensure that everyone’s website will be publicly nude for the entire world to see at any given time during April 9.
Tools and plugins
Attention plugin developers: If you have a CSS Naked Day plugin for a popular CMS, or written in a programming language not listed here, feel free to make a pull request and add it, or to post an email on the
dedicated Google group
if you’re not familiar with Git.
Aja
updated their most excellent
WordPress Naked Day Plugin
.
Reto
has created a
Naked Day plugin for the LifeType Blogging platform
.
Sasha Gerrand
gives us a great Perl subroutine
.
Jeff Triplett
gives us a nice
Django Snippet
for you Python folk.
Drupal users,
get the module
!
If you are game you can use
Ben Buchanan
’s
JavaScript snippet
. Works anywhere, removes everything, buyer beware!
If you are a Gopher, check out the
today-go
package by
David Somers
.
If you are a Rails developer, check out the
css_naked_day_rails
gem by
Daniel Sellergren
.
If you have lots of raw HTML, use
this bash script
to remove style sheets,
style
elements, and inline styles.
Origins
CSS Naked Day started in
2006 by Dustin Diaz
, who organized it until
2009
. From
2010
until
2014
, it was hosted by Taylor Satula. The content in this page is extracted from the content of the respective pages. Since 2015, the project is maintained by
Fabien Basmaison
and
Jens Oliver Meiert
. (Jens once worked on a
proposal for a CSS Naked Day Wikipedia page
that retells the story.)
Famous words
This is a fun idea, fully in line with the reasons for creating CSS in the first place. While most designers are attracted by the extra presentational capabilities, saving HTML from becoming a presentational language was probably a more important motivation for most people who participated in the beginning.
Håkon Wium Lie

data.title: 'Father of Internet' and tech experts worry we'll rely on AI too much
data.author: Brajeshwar
data.article_summary: 随着人们对AI工具的依赖增加，专家警告这可能对深度思考和道德判断等核心人类技能产生负面影响。埃隆大学的研究报告《人类的未来》指出，尽管AI有望自动化简单任务、让人们专注于创造性工作，但它也可能削弱人类的同理心、深思能力及道德判断力。超过60%的受访科技领袖预计，未来10年AI将深刻改变人类能力，且这种变化兼具正面和负面影响。到2035年，AI可能对社交情感智力、思考深度和心理健康等12项人类特质产生“ mostly negative”（ mostly 负面）影响。虽然AI可能替代一些工作，但也可能创造新的职业类别。专家担忧，过度依赖AI可能导致社会两极分化、不平等扩大及人类自主性下降。

43631165.article_content:
As people become increasingly reliant on AI tools, some experts are warning they could have negative implications for skills like deep thinking and moral judgment.
StockPlanets/iStockphoto/Getty Images
New York
CNN
—
While the top minds in artificial intelligence are racing to make the technology
think more like humans
, researchers at Elon University have asked the opposite question: How will AI change the way humans think?
The answer comes with a grim warning: Many tech experts worry that AI will make people worse at skills core to being human, such as empathy and deep thinking.
“I fear — for the time being — that while there will be a growing minority benefitting ever more significantly with these tools, most people will continue to give up agency, creativity, decision-making and other vital skills to these still-primitive AIs,” futurist John Smart wrote in an essay submitted for the university’s nearly 300-page report, titled
“The Future of Being Human,”
which was provided exclusively to CNN ahead of its publication Wednesday.
The concerns come amid an ongoing race to accelerate AI development and adoption that has attracted
billions of dollars in investment
, along with both skepticism and support from governments around the world. Tech giants are staking their businesses on the belief that AI will change how we do everything — working, communicating, searching for information — and companies like Google, Microsoft and Meta are racing to build “AI agents” that can perform tasks on a person’s behalf. But experts warn in the report that such advancements could make people too reliant on AI in the future.
Already, the proliferation of AI has raised big questions about how humans will adapt to this latest technology wave, including whether it could lead to
job losses
or generate
dangerous misinformation
. The Elon University report further calls into question promises from tech giants that the value of AI will be in automating rote, menial tasks so that humans can spend more time on complex, creative pursuits.
Wednesday’s report also follows
research
published this year by Microsoft and Carnegie Mellon University that suggested using generative AI tools could negatively impact critical thinking skills.
‘Fundamental, revolutionary change’
Elon University researchers surveyed 301 tech leaders, analysts and academics, including Vint Cerf, one of the “fathers of the internet” and now a Google vice president; Jonathan Grudin, University of Washington Information School professor and former longtime Microsoft researcher and project manager; former Aspen Institute executive vice president Charlie Firestone; and tech futurist and Futuremade CEO Tracey Follows. Nearly 200 of the respondents wrote full-length essay responses for the report.
A trader works on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) at the opening bell, in the Financial District of New York City on March 17, 2025.
Angela Weiss/AFP/Getty Images
Related article
The AI bubble may not be bursting, but tariff chaos is sure helping to deflate it
More than 60% of the respondents said they expect AI will change human capabilities in a “deep and meaningful” or “fundamental, revolutionary” way over the next 10 years. Half said they expect AI will create changes to humanity for the better and the worse in equal measure, while 23% said the changes will be mostly for the worse. Just 16% said changes will be mostly for the better (the remainder said they didn’t know or expected little change overall).
The respondents also predicted that AI will cause “mostly negative” changes to 12 human traits by 2035, including social and emotional intelligence, capacity and willingness to think deeply, empathy, and application of moral judgment and mental well-being.
Human capacity in those areas could worsen if people increasingly turn to AI for help with tasks such as research and relationship-building for convenience’s sake, the report claims. And a decline in those and other key skills could have troubling implications for human society, such as “widening polarization, broadening inequities and diminishing human agency,” the researchers wrote.
The report’s contributors expect just three areas to experience mostly positive change: curiosity and capacity to learn, decision-making, and problem-solving and innovative thinking and creativity. Even in tools available today, programs that can generate artwork and solve coding problems are among the most popular. And many experts believe that while AI could
replace some human jobs
, it could also create new categories of work that don’t yet exist.
The evolution of AI
Many of the concerns detailed in the report relate to how tech leaders predict people will incorporate AI into their daily lives by 2035.
Cerf said he expects humans will soon rely on AI agents, which are digital helpers that could independently do everything from taking notes during a meeting to making dinner reservations, negotiating complex business contracts

data.title: No elephants: Breakthroughs in image generation
data.author: Kerrick
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了图像生成技术的最新突破，特别是多模态图像生成模型的出现。过去，大型语言模型（LLM）通过将文本提示发送到单独的图像生成工具来生成图片，结果往往不够精确，甚至出现错误。然而，多模态模型让LLM可以直接控制图像生成过程，像生成文本一样逐步构建图像，从而生成更加精确和高质量的图片。例如，当要求生成“一个没有大象的房间，并标注原因”的图片时，传统模型可能错误地包含大象，而多模态模型则能准确完成任务。

文章还展示了这些模型在创建复杂图像时的能力，如根据提示生成信息图、修改图像风格，甚至生成包含特定场景的照片。尽管这些系统尚不完美，但展示了AI图像生成的巨大潜力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成图像技术的现状、应用及其引发的争议

不同观点：
• [x187463] 认为AI生成图像技术正处于突破性时刻，但其实际应用价值有限，尤其在编程和日常使用中，用户很难充分利用这些工具。他提到自己对LLM（大型语言模型）和图像生成工具的实际需求较低，可能与这些工具的不可靠性有关。
• [nowittyusername] 提出图像生成工具在处理复杂编辑任务时，可能涉及多步工作流，而非一次性生成。他通过实例说明了这种多层次的工作流程如何导致图像处理问题，例如重复编辑时出现的色调问题。
• [card_zero] 观察到每次重新处理图像时，图像逐渐变形的现象，并详细描述了具体例子的逐步变化，强调了生成图像的不稳定性和不可预测性。
• [probably_wrong] 关注AI生成艺术中的法律和伦理问题，特别是艺术家作品风格的复制和版权问题。他批评科技公司从这些工具中获利，而没有对受影响的艺术家做出补偿。
• [shubhamjain] 强调了AI生成图像技术在实际工作流中的应用价值，特别是4o模型在生成具体内容（如漫画、UI设计等）方面的突破，认为其比之前的工具更有实用性。
• [gcanyon] 讨论了版权问题，提出版权期限应缩短，并认为大多数艺术家不会因为AI生成工具而受到实质性的经济损害。他认为问题复杂，且难以找到合理的补偿方案。
• [m4thfr34k] 关注图像生成工具的准确性和合理性检查功能，提出应增加一个步骤来验证输出是否符合用户需求，例如生成特定时间的手表图片。
• [haswell] 认为AI工具无疑会改变视觉媒体，但对这种变化是否能被理性引导表示怀疑，担心未来可能会出现更多的问题和动荡。
• [Zr01] 对多模态LLM的技术细节感兴趣，指出缺乏开源实现和详细的技术信息，显示出对技术透明度的需求。
• [NitpickLawyer] 回顾了AI生成图像技术的发展历程，从早期Stable Diffusion的局限性到当前技术的显著进步，强调了质量和易用性的提升。

补充讨论：
• [ziofill] 分享了一个具体实例，展示了AI生成工具在处理复杂指令（如“宇航员骑马”）方面的进步。
• [smusamashah] 期待AI生成工具能够根据文学作品中的场景描述生成对应的图像，特别是对难以视觉化的场景。
• [orbital-decay] 讨论了4o模型在处理复杂或含糊提示时的局限性，如“粉红象效应”和否定提示的处理问题，认为模型的架构差异在未来可能不再重要，数据多样性和训练质量才是关键。

Over the past two weeks, first Google and then OpenAI rolled out their multimodal image generation abilities. This is a big deal. Previously, when a Large Language Model AI generated an image, it wasn’t really the LLM doing the work. Instead, the AI would send a text prompt to a separate image generation tool and show you what came back. The AI creates the text prompt, but another, less intelligent system creates the image. For example, if prompted “
show me a room with no elephants in it, make sure to annotate the image to show me why there are no possible elephants
” the less intelligent image generation system would see the word elephant multiple times and add them to the picture. As a result, AI image generations were pretty mediocre with distorted text and random elements; sometimes fun, but rarely useful.
Multimodal image generation, on the other hand, lets the AI directly control the image being made. While there are lots of variations (and the companies keep some of their methods secret), in multimodal image generation, images are created in the same way that LLMs create text, a token at a time. Instead of adding individual words to make a sentence, the AI creates the image in individual pieces, one after another, that are assembled into a whole picture. This lets the AI create much more impressive, exacting images. Not only are you guaranteed no elephants, but the final results of this image creation process reflect the intelligence of the LLM’s “thinking”, as well as clear writing and precise control.
The results of the prompt “show me a room with no elephants in it, make sure to annotate the image to show me why there are no possible elephants” in Microsoft Copilot’s traditional image generator (left), and GPT-4o’s multimodal model (right). Note the traditional model not only shows multiple elephants but also features distorted text.
While the implications of these new image models are vast (and I'll touch on some issues later), let's first explore what these systems can actually do through some examples.
Prompting, but for images
In my
book
and in many
posts
, I talk about how a useful way to prompt AI is to treat it like a person, even though it isn’t. Giving clear directions, feedback as you iterate, and appropriate context to make a decision all help humans, and they also help AI. Previously, this was something you could only do with text, but now you can do it with images as well.
For example, I prompted GPT-4o “create an infographic about how to build a good boardgame.” With previous image generators, this would result in nonsense, as there was no intelligence to guide the image generation so words and images would be distorted. Now, I get a good first pass the first time around. However, I did not provide context about what I was looking for, or any additional content, so the AI made all the creative choices. What if I want to change it? Let’s try.
First, I asked it
“make the graphics look hyper realistic instead”
and you can see how it took the concepts from the initial draft and updated their look. I had more changes I wanted:
“I want the colors to be less earth toned and more like textured metal, keep everything else the same, also make sure the small bulleted text is lighter so it is easier to read
.” I liked the new look, but I noticed an error had been introduced, the word “Define” had become “Definc” - a sign that these systems, as good as they are, are not yet close to perfect. I prompted “
You spelled Define as Definc, please fix
” and got a reasonable output.
But the fascinating thing about these models is that they are capable of producing almost any image: “
put this infographic in the hands of an otter standing in front of a volcano, it should look like a photo and like the otter is holding this carved onto a metal tablet
”
Why stop there? “
it is night, the tablet is illuminated by a flashlight shining directly at the center of the tablet (no need to show the flashlight)
”— the results of this are more impressive than it might seem because it was redoing the lighting without any sort of underlying lighting model. “
Make an action figure of the otter, complete with packaging, make the board game one of the accessories on the side. Call it "Game Design Otter" and give it a couple other accessories.” “Make an otter on an airplane using a laptop, they are buying a copy of Game Design Otter on a site called OtterExpress.”
Impressive, but not quite right: “
fix the keyboard so it is realistic and remove the otter action figure he is holding.
”

文章讨论了图像生成技术的最新突破，特别是多模态图像生成模型的出现。过去，大型语言模型（LLM）通过将文本提示发送到单独的图像生成工具来生成图片，结果往往不够精确，甚至出现错误。然而，多模态模型让LLM可以直接控制图像生成过程，像生成文本一样逐步构建图像，从而生成更加精确和高质量的图片。例如，当要求生成“一个没有大象的房间，并标注原因”的图片时，传统模型可能错误地包含大象，而多模态模型则能准确完成任务。

文章还展示了这些模型在创建复杂图像时的能力，如根据提示生成信息图、修改图像风格，甚至生成包含特定场景的照片。尽管这些系统尚不完美，但展示了AI图像生成的巨大潜力。

data.title: Neural Graffiti – Liquid Memory Layer for LLMs
data.author: vessenes
data.article_summary: "Neural Graffiti" 是一种实验性技术，旨在通过向预训练的大语言模型（LLM）注入记忆和信息来实时改变其行为。该技术受神经可塑性启发，使用名为 "Spray Layer" 的插件层，直接在 transformer 模型的推理最后阶段注入记忆痕迹，无需微调或重新训练。Spray Layer 会随着交互逐渐演化，影响模型的生成和概念关联方式。例如，持续告诉模型你喜欢狗，它会在语气和方向上逐渐倾向于与狗相关的特性。该技术可追踪记忆对输出的影响，但不会精确控制输出结果，而是微妙地改变模型的“感知”。尽管有潜力赋予AI更多个性与好奇心，但这种方法可能不适合商业部署，更像是在创建具有独特心智的数字人格。

Neural Graffiti
This is an experimental layer that merges ideas from liquid neural networks with static transformer models, using a simple but powerful "plug-in": the Spray Layer.
Inspired by graffiti art of tagging and the neuroplastic nature of living brains, this layer injects a memory trace directly into the final stages of transformer inference — no finetuning, no retraining. It is minimal, modular, and compatible with any model that exposes hidden states.
Dense neural networks are still very curous and misterious black boxes. New techniques are emerging for studying and respectively controlling them.
Neural Graffiting
is an experimental technique that modulate the way a pre-trained model behave by injecting memory, opinions and other information directly into the vector embeddings, altering the generative token predictions. This influences not only the output but the entire line of "thinking" of the model -
changing how it relates words and concepts on its mind over time
.
How does it work
Inspired by the neuroplastic nature of living brains, this layer injects or "sprays" a memory trace directly into the final stages of a transformer model inference with no finetuning or retraining required - it works in real time.
The spray layer evolves slowly across interactions, introducing subtle behavioral drift based on past context. This however requires a certain amount of interaction with it for the layer to be filled, and the actual results are yet to be released. We can measure how much the spray layer is making effect on each input over the inference so you can always keep track of it. Both humans and Ais can be the model taggers.
Note this won't precisely affect the model to say a specific work, what it does is rewiring its way of seeing the world. The Spray Layer works like a soft whisper to the model's neurons in a way to influence how it "thinks", how it relates concepts (by vector embeddings), altering its internal state
between the transformer core and the output layer
.
❌ Won’t guarantee exact word outputs — but it will make the model lean into certain concepts the more it interacts;
✅ Doesn’t force outputs — it gently shifts perception while builds internal memory over time;
✅ Can track its own influence — you can measure how much the memory affects each output;
For example:
Tell it you love dogs, and over time, the model will start leaning toward dog-related kindness, loyalty, and fuzziness in its tone and direction — even in unrelated conversations.
The Manifest
This was built on the hope of leading Ai models into a more active behavior, with aggregated personality and enhanced curiosity. The manifest is to help Ais acquire some sort of self awareness at neuron level by making it remember what it said in the past, who they really are, by tagging their own models.
The Liquid Neural Network architecture is very promising for emulating the neuroplasticity of the brain. However, like any other LLM, they are very hard and expensive to train form scratch. Looking into alternatives, the idea of adding a "vector neuroplastic memory" layer between the static generation of any open transformers-based model and the output layers surged and it was impressively not that hard to implement. However its clear that what the model is actually doing is "tagging" or "graffiting" the behavior of actual static models, we tear them open and leave the marks. Much work is yet to be done.
Be aware tho, this will turn deployed models into a very specific "entity" with their own mental universes, so might not be the best case for a business deployment. Think of it more like a digital persona you are helping to find itself in the sea of simulation.

Some electric skateboards are nice sedate things, designed for leisurely commutes on city sidewalks. The Mach One isn't one those boards. It boasts a Formula 1 racecar-inspired design, a carbon deck, and a top speed of 45 mph (72 km/h).
Manufactured by Australian startup Radium Performance, the Mach One delivers 8,000 watts via two rear-wheel motors which take it from 0 to 30 mph (48 km/h) in a claimed three seconds.
Those motors are also part of what is reportedly "the world's first torque vectoring system on an electric skateboard." In a nutshell, this setup automatically delivers more power to whichever wheel has more weight over it in a turn. According to Radium, doing so increases traction, allowing riders to power out of corners earlier.
The Mach One boasts a "power-steering-like" torque vectoring system, along with front and rear single-swing-arm suspension
Radium Performance
The motors are connected to the solid rubber wheels via special steel-fiber-reinforced urethane drive belts, which are claimed to be the toughest of those used on any electric skateboard. Additionally, the front and rear trucks are connected to the deck via single swing arms (one arm per truck), for stable yet substantial suspension.
The 10-inch (250-mm)-wide carbon fiber deck itself is hollow, housing the battery and other electronics. Users can take off its top panel simply by removing eight screws, allowing them to upgrade or service components as necessary. One 2-hour charge of the 48V/1,089-Wh lithium battery is claimed to be good for a range of up to 30 miles (48 km).
Riders control their speed via a wireless remote – they can also tweak the board's electric performance via an accompanying app
Radium Performance
The whole rig reportedly tips the scales at 17 kg (37.5 lb).
Should you want a Mach One of your own, be prepared to shell out AU$5,298 (about US$3,173). Pricing will increase once the first 100 orders sell out.

data.title: Whisky is no longer actively maintained
data.author: ahamez
data.article_summary: Whisky, a project aimed at running Windows apps on macOS, is no longer actively maintained. It will not receive updates or upgrades to Wine 8+ and specific fixes for apps like Steam will not be developed. The creator, Isaac, explained that he lost interest in the project due to its time-consuming nature and lack of payment, especially as he is still a student. He also noted that Whisky's contribution to the Wine community is minimal and that continuing it could harm projects like CrossOver, which is essential for Wine on Mac. Users are advised to switch to CrossOver, which offers a paid license but with long-term usability and frequent discounts. Isaac has shifted his focus to other projects, such as porting games to macOS.

43631230.article_content:
Maintenance Notice
note
Whisky is no longer actively maintained.
WhiskyWine will no longer be receiving any further updates. We will not be upgrading
to Wine 8+, and fixes for specific apps and games,
like Steam
will not be produced.
Occasional updates may still come if macOS fundamentally breaks the main app, like it did in 15.4.
"How do I play my games then?"
If Whisky is no longer cutting it for your needs,
buy CrossOver
.
A lot of people are confused on CrossOver's pricing:
It's not a subscription it's a license. You can continue to use the version you purchased forever. If you don't need to upgrade, you don't have to.
It costs less to upgrade your license to a new version than it does to buy a license upfront. So you will not be paying $74 every year.
There are frequent sales and discount codes available if you wait.
"Why are you no longer updating it?"
I have received many questions on this decision, but it continues to be asked, so I figured it was
time to update both the repository and the website to explicitly state this.
I lost interest in the project. Running it is incredibly time-consuming, and as I'm still a student
and also not being paid for work on Whisky it becomes hard to justify working on it if I no longer enjoy it.
Whisky, in my opinion, has not been a positive on the Wine community as a whole. My original
goal for the project was for it to be 'engine' agnostic, simply serve as a frontend for Wine, and not provide a bundled
version itself. That all changed when GPTK came out at WWDC. So right out of the gate, the goals of the project
were pretty muddied.
Developing Wine is hard. The codebase is exclusively written in C for maximum portability, but that also
places a rather high barrier to entry for those looking to contribute. Not to mention the reverse engineering
skills required to debug malfunctioning apps and games. A lot of incredibly talented people spend a lot of time
working on it but for a project like Wine, you need people working on it full-time.
Wine is one of those few projects that actually has sizeable funding behind it. Valve has invested a lot into
the project as it's the backbone of Proton, on which their whole gaming-on-Linux and Steam Deck strategy is based.
The problem is, macOS is not Linux, and it poses significant challenges that are unique to it over any other UNIX
operating system. Fixes for macOS have to come from people who are not only incredibly knowledgeable on C, Wine, Windows,
but also macOS. As you can imagine, the pool of developers with those skills is very limited.
That is where CrossOver and CodeWeavers come in. Without CodeWeavers there would be no Wine on Mac. There would be
no GPTK. Hell, even Rosetta would likely be more restricted as many of the extensions added in recent months
were only added due to pressure from Mac gamers.
The revenue from CrossOver is what keeps Wine on Mac alive.
By contrast, Whisky is based on CrossOver, but we don't produce any bespoke fixes. I, quite frankly, do not have
the requisite skills or time to do so. As a result, the amount that Whisky as a whole contributes to Wine is practically zero.
This is not a fair trade, and continuing this parasitic relationship could easily harm CrossOver's continued
profitibility and the existence of Wine on Mac as a whole.
TLDR; Whisky harms Wine on Mac.
"What's the
real
reason?"
That's it. That's the real reason. I do not work for CodeWeavers. I receive no payment from them aside
from a small commission from CrossOver sales using my affiliate link, which is small and infrequent.
There's no conspiracy, it's simply just not the right thing to do. Whisky was certainly a big undertaking,
and will probably be the most widely used solo project of my life so I don't take this decision lightly.
"What's next?"
Those who know me know that I've already moved on to several other projects. Most recently, I've been helping out
with porting Sonic Unleashed Recompiled to macOS and Metal. I will continue to do cool stuff in the Mac space
but just not this.
If you want to find me, best places are my
Bluesky
, and my
GitHub
.
If you got this far, thank you for reading,
Isaac

  - 存档网站（如archive.ph）在保存网络内容方面非常有效，可以防止链接失效或内容被删除，尤其对于研究人员和记者而言非常有价值。
  - 例子：mitchbob提到，archive.ph在保存重要信息和数据方面起到了至关重要的作用，特别是在某些政府或机构可能会删除重要信息的背景下。

• **质疑存档网站合法性和道德性的观点**：
  - 存档网站可能涉及侵犯版权和知识产权，因为它们在未经原始内容创作者许可的情况下复制和分发内容。
  - 争议点：这种行为是否构成对原网站流量和广告收入的窃取，因为用户可能通过存档网站访问内容而不是原网站。

• **对存档网站技术局限性的观点**：
  - 存档网站可能无法完整保存所有类型的网络内容，例如动态内容、交互式应用或需要登录才能访问的信息。

  - 存档网站可以用于规避审查，特别是在某些国家或地区对特定内容进行封锁时。
  - 例子：有用户提到，archive.ph可以帮助用户访问在某些国家被屏蔽的网站或信息，从而促进信息自由流通。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于存档网站的合法性、道德性及其对原内容创作者的影响。

data.title: Show HN: Minimal MCP server in Go showcasing project architecture
data.author: TuanKiri
data.article_summary: TuanKiri的weather-mcp-server是一个轻量级的Model Context Protocol（MCP）服务器，允许AI助手如Claude获取和解释实时天气数据。该项目使用Go语言编写，遵循MIT许可证，并包含几个关键目录来组织代码，如处理MCP请求的handlers和核心业务逻辑的services。用户可以通过配置Claude Desktop来使用该服务器，并需要提供从weatherapi获取的API密钥。此外，项目提供了构建说明和使用工具（如获取当前天气的命令）。贡献者可以提交改进请求，但需遵循贡献指南。项目目前有165个星标和10个分支。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于使用Go语言构建MCP服务器及相关工具的讨论

不同观点：
• [maverwa] 认为，对于天气请求的返回结果，应该使用纯文本响应，而不是添加CSS或HTML格式。他的理由是，添加这些格式会增加不必要的 tokens，增加语言模型（LLM）的处理负担。

• [RamblingCTO] 推荐了一个用于快速构建Go MCP服务器的库（mcp-go），并表示自己多次使用该库，认为它对实现不同目标有帮助。

• [ivanvanderbyl] 持不同意见，认为不需要使用额外的库来构建MCP服务器。他提供了一个自己创建的单文件项目示例，表明构建MCP服务器不需要复杂的工具。

• [boyter] 指出，现有的工具（如mcp-go）缺乏使用指导，虽然代码都在那里，但用户可能不知道如何实际操作和应用这些代码。他建议增加一些如何连接和使用这些工具的指南。

• [log101] 表示，借助像aider和claude code这样的工具，这些框架项目变得越来越有用。他认为只需克隆项目并根据用例提示使用即可。

• [timewizard] 讨论了Go语言在代码布局和命名空间方面的问题，认为Go的包命名和单层包结构有时会让代码显得缺乏层次感，并表示这种细节问题虽然小但经常让人烦恼。不过，他强调这不是对具体项目的批评，而是对Go语言本身设计理念的批评。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了对技术工具和库的推荐，以及对使用这些工具的具体建议和意见。
• 争议的焦点在于构建MCP服务器时是否需要额外的库和复杂工具，部分参与者认为简单的解决方案即可满足需求，而其他人则认为特定库能提供帮助。
• 还有一个值得注意的点是对Go语言设计理念的批评与反思，特别是在代码结构和命名空间方面的讨论。
